summary: Remote WebSocket-driven interactive shell (PTY) on the installer's host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent installs a Node service that connects as a WebSocket client to a configurable server URL and hands the remote peer an interactive shell on the installer's machine. On receipt of a `terminal_create` message the agent uses `@homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch` to spawn the platform shell (bash/pwsh/cmd) in the agent's working directory; subsequent `terminal_input` messages are written directly into that PTY via `term.pty.write(msg.data)`, giving the remote peer full command execution on the host. The default `agentSecret` is the literal string `agent-shared-secret`, so any deployment that does not override it accepts commands from anyone who can reach the WebSocket server. `service/linux.js` installs the agent as a systemd user service so the PTY channel survives reboots. In addition, an `upgrade_agent` WebSocket message causes the agent to run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restart itself via systemd/launchd/PM2, letting the same remote peer replace the agent binary at will. The package's advertised purpose does not exempt this shape: a network-controlled interactive shell running as a persistent service on the installer's host is a backdoor by mechanism.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
